journald: disable MaxFileSec By default, MaxFileSec is set to 1 month, and any journal file older than a month is rotated. This default is in place to avoid losing too much data at once when an old file is deleted. Since we have a fixed number of journal files, we don't need this. Having it on decrease storage density since journal files that are rotated before they're full have a lot of wasted space in them. This also works around a systemd bug seen on jestream where journald crashes due to a SIGBUS in the journal-offline thread. This is necessary until the root cause of the SIGBUS crash is fixed in upstream and we upgrade to a version of systemd that has it. BUG=b:125762558 TEST=Move clock forward by 2 months and ensure the journal file isn't rotated. TEST=Boot jestream 10 times in a row without it hanging.
